question: Which customers have never placed an order? Return customer_id and full_name.
reference_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name FROM customers AS c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders AS o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id)

question: How many customers live in Tunisia? Return one number.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers WHERE country = 'Tunisia'

question: Which five active products have the lowest list price? Return product_id, product_name, and list_price_cents, ordered by price from lowest to highest and then by product_id.
reference_sql: SELECT product_id, product_name, list_price_cents FROM products WHERE is_active = 1 ORDER BY list_price_cents ASC, product_id ASC LIMIT 5

question: Which customers have at least three completed orders? Return customer_id, full_name, and the number of completed orders. Sort by that number from highest to lowest, then by customer_id.
reference_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, COUNT(*) AS completed_order_count FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3 ORDER BY completed_order_count DESC, c.customer_id ASC

question: Which customer-product pairs bought the same product in at least two different completed orders? Return customer_id and product_id, sorted by customer_id and then product_id.
reference_sql: SELECT o.customer_id, i.product_id FROM orders AS o JOIN order_items AS i ON i.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.customer_id, i.product_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) >= 2 ORDER BY o.customer_id ASC, i.product_id ASC

question: How many orders were placed during August 2026? Return one number.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE ordered_at >= '2026-08-01' AND ordered_at < '2026-09-01'

question: Which countries have at least one active customer? Return each country once, sorted alphabetically.
reference_sql: SELECT DISTINCT country FROM customers WHERE is_active = 1 ORDER BY country ASC

question: How many completed orders had at least one failed payment attempt? Return one number.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) FROM orders AS o JOIN payments AS p ON p.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND p.status = 'failed'

question: For each customer country, what is the total amount of successful payments in cents? Return country and total_successful_cents. Sort by total from highest to lowest, then by country.
reference_sql: SELECT c.country, SUM(p.amount_cents) AS total_successful_cents FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN payments AS p ON p.order_id = o.order_id WHERE p.status = 'successful' GROUP BY c.country ORDER BY total_successful_cents DESC, c.country ASC

question: For each category, what is the average list price in cents of its active products? Return category_name and average_price_cents, sorted alphabetically by category name.
reference_sql: SELECT ca.category_name, AVG(p.list_price_cents) AS average_price_cents FROM categories AS ca JOIN products AS p ON p.category_id = ca.category_id WHERE p.is_active = 1 GROUP BY ca.category_id, ca.category_name ORDER BY ca.category_name ASC

question: Which products have never appeared in a completed order? Return product_id and product_name, sorted by product_id.
reference_sql: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name FROM products AS p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items AS i JOIN orders AS o ON o.order_id = i.order_id WHERE i.product_id = p.product_id AND o.status = 'completed') ORDER BY p.product_id ASC

question: Which completed orders have every purchased unit returned? Return order_id, sorted from lowest to highest.
reference_sql: SELECT o.order_id FROM orders AS o JOIN order_items AS i ON i.order_id = o.order_id LEFT JOIN returns AS r ON r.order_id = i.order_id AND r.line_no = i.line_no WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.order_id HAVING SUM(COALESCE(r.quantity, 0)) = SUM(i.quantity) ORDER BY o.order_id ASC

question: Which inactive customers live in France? Return customer_id and full_name, sorted by customer_id.
reference_sql: SELECT customer_id, full_name FROM customers WHERE country = 'France' AND is_active = 0 ORDER BY customer_id ASC

question: How many cancelled orders were placed during August 2026? Return one number.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled' AND ordered_at >= '2026-08-01' AND ordered_at < '2026-09-01'

question: What are the minimum and maximum list prices in cents among active products? Return min_price_cents and max_price_cents.
reference_sql: SELECT MIN(list_price_cents) AS min_price_cents, MAX(list_price_cents) AS max_price_cents FROM products WHERE is_active = 1

question: Which customers in Morocco joined before January 1, 2026? Return customer_id, full_name, and joined_at. Sort by joined_at, then customer_id.
reference_sql: SELECT customer_id, full_name, joined_at FROM customers WHERE country = 'Morocco' AND joined_at < '2026-01-01' ORDER BY joined_at ASC, customer_id ASC

question: Which placed orders have no completion date? Return order_id and customer_id, sorted by order_id.
reference_sql: SELECT order_id, customer_id FROM orders WHERE status = 'placed' AND completed_at IS NULL ORDER BY order_id ASC

question: Which inactive products have a list price greater than 10000 cents? Return product_id, product_name, and list_price_cents. Sort by price from highest to lowest, then product_id.
reference_sql: SELECT product_id, product_name, list_price_cents FROM products WHERE is_active = 0 AND list_price_cents > 10000 ORDER BY list_price_cents DESC, product_id ASC

question: How many placed orders were created before April 1, 2026? Return one number.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE status = 'placed' AND ordered_at < '2026-04-01'

question: Which cities in France have at least one active customer? Return each city once, sorted alphabetically.
reference_sql: SELECT DISTINCT city FROM customers WHERE country = 'France' AND is_active = 1 ORDER BY city ASC

question: Which active products cost between 3000 and 7000 cents, inclusive? Return product_id, product_name, and list_price_cents, sorted by product_name and then product_id.
reference_sql: SELECT product_id, product_name, list_price_cents FROM products WHERE is_active = 1 AND list_price_cents BETWEEN 3000 AND 7000 ORDER BY product_name ASC, product_id ASC

question: What are the five most recently completed orders? Return order_id and completed_at, sorted by completed_at from newest to oldest, then by order_id from highest to lowest.
reference_sql: SELECT order_id, completed_at FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' ORDER BY completed_at DESC, order_id DESC LIMIT 5

question: What is the average quantity per order-item line where the unit price is at least 5000 cents? Return one number.
reference_sql: SELECT AVG(quantity) FROM order_items WHERE unit_price_cents >= 5000

question: How many distinct customers have at least one cancelled order? Return one number.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled'

question: Which failed payment attempts had an attempted amount greater than 20000 cents? Return payment_id, order_id, and amount_cents. Sort by amount from highest to lowest, then payment_id.
reference_sql: SELECT payment_id, order_id, amount_cents FROM payments WHERE status = 'failed' AND amount_cents > 20000 ORDER BY amount_cents DESC, payment_id ASC

question: How many order-item lines have a quantity of exactly five? Return one number.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM order_items WHERE quantity = 5

question: Which returns have the reason 'damaged'? Return return_id, order_id, and quantity, sorted by return_id.
reference_sql: SELECT return_id, order_id, quantity FROM returns WHERE reason = 'damaged' ORDER BY return_id ASC

question: What are the earliest and latest join dates among inactive customers? Return earliest_date and latest_date.
reference_sql: SELECT MIN(joined_at) AS earliest_date, MAX(joined_at) AS latest_date FROM customers WHERE is_active = 0

question: What are the five oldest orders still marked placed? Return order_id and ordered_at, sorted by ordered_at from oldest to newest, then order_id.
reference_sql: SELECT order_id, ordered_at FROM orders WHERE status = 'placed' ORDER BY ordered_at ASC, order_id ASC LIMIT 5

question: How many distinct products appear on order-item lines with quantity at least three? Return one number.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT product_id) FROM order_items WHERE quantity >= 3

question: For every customer, how many orders have they placed, including cancelled orders? Return customer_id, full_name, and order_count. Include customers with zero orders and sort by customer_id.
reference_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers AS c LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name ORDER BY c.customer_id ASC

question: For each category, how many active products does it contain? Return category_name and active_product_count. Include categories with zero active products; sort by count from highest to lowest, then category name.
reference_sql: SELECT ca.category_name, COUNT(p.product_id) AS active_product_count FROM categories AS ca LEFT JOIN products AS p ON p.category_id = ca.category_id AND p.is_active = 1 GROUP BY ca.category_id, ca.category_name ORDER BY active_product_count DESC, ca.category_name ASC

question: What is the item total in cents for each completed order placed during August 2026? Return order_id and order_total_cents. Sort by total from highest to lowest, then order_id.
reference_sql: SELECT o.order_id, SUM(i.quantity * i.unit_price_cents) AS order_total_cents FROM orders AS o JOIN order_items AS i ON i.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND o.ordered_at >= '2026-08-01' AND o.ordered_at < '2026-09-01' GROUP BY o.order_id ORDER BY order_total_cents DESC, o.order_id ASC

question: How many completed orders were placed by customers in each country? Return country and completed_order_count, sorted by country.
reference_sql: SELECT c.country, COUNT(o.order_id) AS completed_order_count FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.country ORDER BY c.country ASC

question: Which products appear in at least five different orders, regardless of order status? Return product_id, product_name, and order_count. Sort by count from highest to lowest, then product_id.
reference_sql: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, COUNT(DISTINCT i.order_id) AS order_count FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS i ON i.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT i.order_id) >= 5 ORDER BY order_count DESC, p.product_id ASC

question: For each product category, how many order-item lines belong to completed orders? Return category_name and line_count. Sort by count from highest to lowest, then category name.
reference_sql: SELECT ca.category_name, COUNT(i.line_no) AS line_count FROM categories AS ca JOIN products AS p ON p.category_id = ca.category_id JOIN order_items AS i ON i.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON o.order_id = i.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY ca.category_id, ca.category_name ORDER BY line_count DESC, ca.category_name ASC

question: How many cancelled orders were placed in each month? Return month in YYYY-MM format and cancelled_order_count, sorted by month.
reference_sql: SELECT SUBSTR(ordered_at, 1, 7) AS month, COUNT(*) AS cancelled_order_count FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled' GROUP BY SUBSTR(ordered_at, 1, 7) ORDER BY month ASC

question: For each order status, how many item units were ordered in total? Return status and total_units, sorted by status. Include items in placed, completed, and cancelled orders.
reference_sql: SELECT o.status, SUM(i.quantity) AS total_units FROM orders AS o JOIN order_items AS i ON i.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY o.status ORDER BY o.status ASC

question: Which customers in Sfax have at least two orders, regardless of status? Return customer_id, full_name, and order_count. Sort by count from highest to lowest, then customer_id.
reference_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.city = 'Sfax' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) >= 2 ORDER BY order_count DESC, c.customer_id ASC

question: For each customer city with at least one failed payment attempt, how many failed attempts came from that city's customers' orders? Return city and failed_attempt_count, sorted by count from highest to lowest, then city.
reference_sql: SELECT c.city, COUNT(p.payment_id) AS failed_attempt_count FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN payments AS p ON p.order_id = o.order_id WHERE p.status = 'failed' GROUP BY c.city ORDER BY failed_attempt_count DESC, c.city ASC

question: For every customer, how many successful payment records belong to their orders? Return customer_id, full_name, and successful_payment_count. Include customers with zero successful payments and sort by customer_id.
reference_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, COUNT(p.payment_id) AS successful_payment_count FROM customers AS c LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id LEFT JOIN payments AS p ON p.order_id = o.order_id AND p.status = 'successful' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name ORDER BY c.customer_id ASC

question: For each category with at least one returned item, how many item units were returned in total? Return category_name and returned_units. Sort by returned_units from highest to lowest, then category name.
reference_sql: SELECT ca.category_name, SUM(r.quantity) AS returned_units FROM categories AS ca JOIN products AS p ON p.category_id = ca.category_id JOIN order_items AS i ON i.product_id = p.product_id JOIN returns AS r ON r.order_id = i.order_id AND r.line_no = i.line_no GROUP BY ca.category_id, ca.category_name ORDER BY returned_units DESC, ca.category_name ASC

question: For each return reason with at least one partial return, how many partial-return records have that reason? A return is partial when fewer units were returned than purchased. Return reason and partial_return_count, sorted by reason.
reference_sql: SELECT r.reason, COUNT(*) AS partial_return_count FROM returns AS r JOIN order_items AS i ON i.order_id = r.order_id AND i.line_no = r.line_no WHERE r.quantity < i.quantity GROUP BY r.reason ORDER BY r.reason ASC

question: Which completed orders contain at least four different products? Return order_id and product_count, sorted by order_id.
reference_sql: SELECT o.order_id, COUNT(DISTINCT i.product_id) AS product_count FROM orders AS o JOIN order_items AS i ON i.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.order_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT i.product_id) >= 4 ORDER BY o.order_id ASC

question: For each customer country, what is the average quantity on order-item lines in completed orders? Return country and average_quantity, sorted by country.
reference_sql: SELECT c.country, AVG(i.quantity) AS average_quantity FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items AS i ON i.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.country ORDER BY c.country ASC

question: For every customer, how many item units are in their completed orders? Return customer_id, full_name, and completed_units. Include customers with zero completed units and sort by customer_id.
reference_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, COALESCE(SUM(i.quantity), 0) AS completed_units FROM customers AS c LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND o.status = 'completed' LEFT JOIN order_items AS i ON i.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name ORDER BY c.customer_id ASC

question: For each category, what is the highest list price in cents among its active products, and how many active products does it have? Return category_name, highest_price_cents, and active_product_count, sorted by category name.
reference_sql: SELECT ca.category_name, MAX(p.list_price_cents) AS highest_price_cents, COUNT(p.product_id) AS active_product_count FROM categories AS ca JOIN products AS p ON p.category_id = ca.category_id WHERE p.is_active = 1 GROUP BY ca.category_id, ca.category_name ORDER BY ca.category_name ASC

question: For each order status, how many distinct customers have an order with that status? Return status and customer_count, sorted by status.
reference_sql: SELECT status, COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS customer_count FROM orders GROUP BY status ORDER BY status ASC

question: For each customer city with returned items, how many return records belong to that city's customers? Return city and return_count. Sort by count from highest to lowest, then city.
reference_sql: SELECT c.city, COUNT(r.return_id) AS return_count FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN returns AS r ON r.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY c.city ORDER BY return_count DESC, c.city ASC

question: For each order status, how many successful and failed payment records belong to orders with that status? Return order_status, successful_count, and failed_count, sorted by order_status.
reference_sql: SELECT o.status AS order_status, SUM(CASE WHEN p.status = 'successful' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS successful_count, SUM(CASE WHEN p.status = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failed_count FROM orders AS o LEFT JOIN payments AS p ON p.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY o.status ORDER BY o.status ASC

question: Which customers have at least one cancelled order but no completed orders? Return customer_id and full_name, sorted by customer_id.
reference_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name FROM customers AS c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders AS x WHERE x.customer_id = c.customer_id AND x.status = 'cancelled') AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders AS y WHERE y.customer_id = c.customer_id AND y.status = 'completed') ORDER BY c.customer_id ASC

question: Which customers have more completed orders than cancelled orders? Return customer_id and full_name, sorted by customer_id.
reference_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN o.status = 'completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > SUM(CASE WHEN o.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ORDER BY c.customer_id ASC

question: Which products were bought in completed orders by customers from at least two different countries? Return product_id, product_name, and country_count. Sort by country_count from highest to lowest, then product_id.
reference_sql: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, COUNT(DISTINCT c.country) AS country_count FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS i ON i.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON o.order_id = i.order_id JOIN customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.country) >= 2 ORDER BY country_count DESC, p.product_id ASC

question: Which customers have a completed order with a failed payment attempt and also a different completed order with no failed payment attempts? Return customer_id and full_name, sorted by customer_id.
reference_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name FROM customers AS c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders AS o1 WHERE o1.customer_id = c.customer_id AND o1.status = 'completed' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM payments AS p1 WHERE p1.order_id = o1.order_id AND p1.status = 'failed')) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders AS o2 WHERE o2.customer_id = c.customer_id AND o2.status = 'completed' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM payments AS p2 WHERE p2.order_id = o2.order_id AND p2.status = 'failed')) ORDER BY c.customer_id ASC

question: Which customers have a completed order whose item total exceeds 100000 cents? Return customer_id, full_name, and their largest completed order total in cents. Sort by that total from highest to lowest, then customer_id.
reference_sql: WITH order_totals AS (SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, SUM(i.quantity * i.unit_price_cents) AS total_cents FROM orders AS o JOIN order_items AS i ON i.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.order_id, o.customer_id) SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, MAX(t.total_cents) AS largest_total_cents FROM customers AS c JOIN order_totals AS t ON t.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name HAVING MAX(t.total_cents) > 100000 ORDER BY largest_total_cents DESC, c.customer_id ASC

question: Which completed orders have at least one partially returned item line but no fully returned item lines? Return order_id, sorted by order_id.
reference_sql: SELECT o.order_id FROM orders AS o WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM returns AS r JOIN order_items AS i ON i.order_id = r.order_id AND i.line_no = r.line_no WHERE r.order_id = o.order_id AND r.quantity < i.quantity) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM returns AS r JOIN order_items AS i ON i.order_id = r.order_id AND i.line_no = r.line_no WHERE r.order_id = o.order_id AND r.quantity = i.quantity) ORDER BY o.order_id ASC

question: Which three customers spent the most on item totals in completed orders, before returns? Return customer_id, full_name, and total_spent_cents. Sort by total from highest to lowest, then customer_id.
reference_sql: WITH customer_spend AS (SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, SUM(i.quantity * i.unit_price_cents) AS total_spent_cents FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items AS i ON i.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name) SELECT customer_id, full_name, total_spent_cents FROM customer_spend ORDER BY total_spent_cents DESC, customer_id ASC LIMIT 3

question: Which customers bought at least one product in two or more different completed orders and also bought at least one other product in exactly one completed order? Return customer_id and full_name, sorted by customer_id.
reference_sql: WITH purchase_counts AS (SELECT o.customer_id, i.product_id, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS purchase_count FROM orders AS o JOIN order_items AS i ON i.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.customer_id, i.product_id) SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name FROM customers AS c JOIN purchase_counts AS pc ON pc.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN pc.purchase_count >= 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) >= 1 AND SUM(CASE WHEN pc.purchase_count = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) >= 1 ORDER BY c.customer_id ASC

question: Which products have appeared in an order but have never had any units returned? Return product_id and product_name, sorted by product_id.
reference_sql: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name FROM products AS p WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items AS i WHERE i.product_id = p.product_id) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM returns AS r JOIN order_items AS i ON i.order_id = r.order_id AND i.line_no = r.line_no WHERE i.product_id = p.product_id) ORDER BY p.product_id ASC

question: Which customers had a cancelled first order and later placed a completed order? Define first and later by ordered_at, breaking same-date ties by order_id. Return customer_id and full_name, sorted by customer_id.
reference_sql: WITH ranked_orders AS (SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, o.ordered_at, o.status, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY o.customer_id ORDER BY o.ordered_at ASC, o.order_id ASC) AS rn FROM orders AS o) SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name FROM customers AS c JOIN ranked_orders AS first_o ON first_o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND first_o.rn = 1 WHERE first_o.status = 'cancelled' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders AS later_o WHERE later_o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND later_o.status = 'completed' AND (later_o.ordered_at > first_o.ordered_at OR (later_o.ordered_at = first_o.ordered_at AND later_o.order_id > first_o.order_id))) ORDER BY c.customer_id ASC

question: Which orders have at least one successful payment but their total successful payments are still less than their item total? Return order_id, order_total_cents, and paid_cents, sorted by order_id.
reference_sql: WITH item_totals AS (SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity * unit_price_cents) AS order_total_cents FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id), paid_totals AS (SELECT order_id, SUM(amount_cents) AS paid_cents FROM payments WHERE status = 'successful' GROUP BY order_id) SELECT i.order_id, i.order_total_cents, p.paid_cents FROM item_totals AS i JOIN paid_totals AS p ON p.order_id = i.order_id WHERE p.paid_cents < i.order_total_cents ORDER BY i.order_id ASC

question: Which category has the highest ratio of returned units to units bought in completed orders? Return category_name, returned_units, and bought_units. Break ratio ties by category_id.
reference_sql: WITH bought AS (SELECT p.category_id, SUM(i.quantity) AS bought_units FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS i ON i.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON o.order_id = i.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category_id), returned AS (SELECT p.category_id, SUM(r.quantity) AS returned_units FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS i ON i.product_id = p.product_id JOIN returns AS r ON r.order_id = i.order_id AND r.line_no = i.line_no GROUP BY p.category_id) SELECT ca.category_name, COALESCE(r.returned_units, 0) AS returned_units, b.bought_units FROM categories AS ca JOIN bought AS b ON b.category_id = ca.category_id LEFT JOIN returned AS r ON r.category_id = ca.category_id ORDER BY 1.0 * COALESCE(r.returned_units, 0) / b.bought_units DESC, ca.category_id ASC LIMIT 1

question: In each country, which customer spent the most on item totals in completed orders, before returns? Return country, customer_id, full_name, and total_spent_cents. Break spending ties by lower customer_id; sort the final rows by country.
reference_sql: WITH spend AS (SELECT c.country, c.customer_id, c.full_name, SUM(i.quantity * i.unit_price_cents) AS total_spent_cents FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items AS i ON i.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.country, c.customer_id, c.full_name), ranked AS (SELECT country, customer_id, full_name, total_spent_cents, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY total_spent_cents DESC, customer_id ASC) AS rn FROM spend) SELECT country, customer_id, full_name, total_spent_cents FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY country ASC

question: Which completed orders contain only products that are currently inactive? Return order_id, sorted by order_id.
reference_sql: SELECT o.order_id FROM orders AS o WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items AS i JOIN products AS p ON p.product_id = i.product_id WHERE i.order_id = o.order_id AND p.is_active = 1) ORDER BY o.order_id ASC

question: Which customer-product pairs bought the product in at least two different completed orders and had at least one return of that product from one of their completed orders? Return customer_id and product_id, sorted by both IDs.
reference_sql: WITH repeated AS (SELECT o.customer_id, i.product_id FROM orders AS o JOIN order_items AS i ON i.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.customer_id, i.product_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) >= 2) SELECT rp.customer_id, rp.product_id FROM repeated AS rp WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM returns AS r JOIN order_items AS i ON i.order_id = r.order_id AND i.line_no = r.line_no JOIN orders AS o ON o.order_id = i.order_id WHERE o.customer_id = rp.customer_id AND i.product_id = rp.product_id AND o.status = 'completed') ORDER BY rp.customer_id ASC, rp.product_id ASC

question: Which category has the largest difference between item totals in completed orders and item totals in cancelled orders? Return category_name, completed_cents, and cancelled_cents. Break difference ties by lower category_id.
reference_sql: WITH totals AS (SELECT p.category_id, SUM(CASE WHEN o.status = 'completed' THEN i.quantity * i.unit_price_cents ELSE 0 END) AS completed_cents, SUM(CASE WHEN o.status = 'cancelled' THEN i.quantity * i.unit_price_cents ELSE 0 END) AS cancelled_cents FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS i ON i.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON o.order_id = i.order_id GROUP BY p.category_id) SELECT ca.category_name, t.completed_cents, t.cancelled_cents FROM categories AS ca JOIN totals AS t ON t.category_id = ca.category_id ORDER BY (t.completed_cents - t.cancelled_cents) DESC, ca.category_id ASC LIMIT 1
